cosy-lesson.title: "Let us read, and let us dance, those two amusements will never do any harm to the world.": Voltaire

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: to introduce the topic and clarify key target vocabulary for the session.

cosy-slide.cosy-instruction: Review the key vocabulary for this session below:

cosy-blockquote.p: Artistry – creative skill or ability in a fine art or literature.

p.em: Example: The novel is praised for its exceptional prose and delicate artistry.

cosy-blockquote.p: Interpretation – the action of explaining the meaning of something.

p.em: Example: There are many different interpretations of this complex, symbolic painting.

cosy-blockquote.p: Aesthetics – a set of principles concerned with the nature and appreciation of beauty.

p.em: Example: The cafe's minimalist aesthetics created a calm, relaxing atmosphere.

cosy-blockquote.p: Inspiration – the process of being mentally stimulated to do or feel something creative.

p.em: Example: Nature has always been the primary source of inspiration for poets.

cosy-blockquote.p: Expression – the action of making known one's thoughts or feelings.

p.em: Example: Music is a powerful form of self-expression for people of all ages.

cosy-blockquote.p: Imagination – the faculty or action of forming new ideas, or images of external objects.

p.em: Example: Children possess a vivid imagination that should never be suppressed.

cosy-blockquote.p: Paraphrase – express the meaning of something using different words.

p.em: Example: To check your understanding, try to paraphrase the author's main argument.

cosy-blockquote.p: Sincerity – the quality of being free from pretense, deceit, or hypocrisy.

p.em: Example: The absolute sincerity of his work made it deeply moving for readers.

cosy-blockquote.p: Ambiguity – the quality of being open to more than one interpretation.

p.em: Example: The poem's rich ambiguity allows each reader to find their own meaning.

cosy-blockquote.p: Originality – the ability to think independently and creatively.

p.em: Example: The artist was celebrated for the fresh originality of her style.

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: pair/group discussion on core session themes.

cosy-slide.cosy-group-instruction: In pairs or small breakout groups, discuss the following questions:

ol.li:
How can daily habits of reading and dancing nurture our personal artistry and intellectual freedom?
★ When was the last time a book or a dance performance inspired your own artistry?

Why does Voltaire suggest that lighthearted amusements require no complex interpretation to bring joy?
★ Do you prefer literature and art that require deep interpretation, or simple unpretentious entertainment?

How do reading and physical movement combine to refine our personal aesthetics and appreciation of life?
★ What role do visual aesthetics play when you choose a book to read or a place to dance?

In what ways can spontaneous joy act as a constant source of creative inspiration in modern society?
★ Where do you usually find your strongest inspiration when you need a mental reset?

How does dancing allow for a pure form of emotional expression that words often fail to capture?
★ Is physical movement like dancing an easy form of expression for you, or do you prefer writing?

Why is an active imagination essential for enjoying literature and uninhibited dance?
★ How often do you let your imagination wander while reading a captivating novel?

How can we paraphrase Voltaire's view on harmless pleasures in the context of today's digital distractions?
★ If you had to paraphrase your philosophy of fun to a friend, what would you emphasize?

Does the sincerity of simple pastimes make them more valuable than elaborate social achievements?
★ How do you express sincerity when sharing your favorite books or music with others?

How does Voltaire eliminate ambiguity regarding the harmless, uplifting nature of reading and dancing?
★ Do you feel comfortable with ambiguity in modern art, or do you prefer clear messages?

In what ways does personal originality flourish when we engage in harmless, unconstrained creative outlets?
★ What is one activity where your personal originality shines brightest?

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: collaborative task or visual analysis in pairs/groups.

cosy-slide.cosy-group-instruction: In pairs, work together on the following task:

cosy-blockquote.p: A comparative reflection on our habits and self-perceptions.

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: 1-on-1 guided visual description and task response with teacher.

cosy-slide.cosy-instruction: Look at the prompt and discuss your response with your teacher:

cosy-blockquote.p: A comparative reflection on our habits and self-perceptions.

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: deeper debate and statement evaluation in pairs/groups.

cosy-slide.cosy-group-instruction: In pairs, debate and state whether you agree or disagree with these statements:

ol.li:
In the future, digitized entertainment will diminish our capacity to appreciate the simple artistry of reading and dancing. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ Would you participate in virtual reality dancing if it felt identical to real-world artistry?

Future societies will view literary interpretation as a vital defense against algorithmic superficiality. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ Would you rely on AI to summarize books if it saved time for personal interpretation?

Modern life prioritizes digital efficiency over the gentle aesthetics of reading and physical dance. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ Do you think your environment's aesthetics encourage you to read more often?

Algorithmic recommendations will eventually replace organic inspiration drawn from books and music. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ Have you ever felt that a digital recommendation gave you genuine inspiration?

Physical dance will remain the ultimate unfiltered form of human expression in an automated world. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ Would you feel comfortable dancing in public as a free form of expression?

Excessive screen time actively stifles the natural imagination cultivated by immersive reading. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ Do you worry that modern technology is weakening your own imagination?

Future generations will prefer to paraphrase classic literature rather than reading full original texts. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ Would you read a shorter version of a classic novel if you didn't have time to paraphrase it yourself?

Genuine sincerity in art will become a rare commodity in an era dominated by viral trends. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ Can you easily detect a lack of sincerity in popular media today?

Embracing ambiguity in leisure activities leads to greater psychological resilience and open-mindedness. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ How do you react when a story ends with complete ambiguity?

True originality is impossible without first immersing oneself in classic literature and culture. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ Do you believe your tastes in music and books reflect true originality?

ul.li: Incorrect: He have went to Paris → Correct: He has gone to Paris ((Present perfect third-person singular 'has' + past participle 'gone'.))

Incorrect: We discussed about the problem → Correct: We discussed the problem / had a discussion about the problem (('Discuss' is transitive and takes no preposition, or use 'have a discussion about'.))
Incorrect: I am agree with you → Correct: I agree with you ((Use 'agree' directly as a verb rather than using it with the auxiliary 'am'.))
